description.narrative: The mission of the Sowing Diversity = Harvesting Security Program of Oxfam Novib and partners is to support indigenous peoples and smallholder farmers – men, women and youth – for them to enjoy their Farmers’ Rights and to have the capacity to access, develop anduse plant genetic resources to improve their food and nutrition security under conditions of climate change. In eight countries we work together with the world’s leading civil society organizations. Our work focuses on four goals: 1. Farmer’s crop improvement andadaptation; 2. Farmer Seed Enterprises; 3. Nutrition and local food plants; 4. An enabling policy environment Funds of private donors are being used to complement the work of the SD=HS program in selected countries. Often this is donethrough Community Seed Banks (CSB) that can form the center of agricultural activities in a community with storage, distribution and sales of seeds, education, further development and demonstration of crop rotation and distribution of water. An importantchallenge some Community Seed Banks arefacing is the lack of electricity and equipment. Ensuring this is taken care of will positively impact the use of the facilities and position of the CSB in the community as a hub for different social and economic activities. The funding of KRAMP will be spent on supporting CSB managed by CTDT in Zambia with solar panels, ensuring they are no longer dependent on the electricity network and equipment to improve distribution activities.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam in Zambia is registered under legal personality of Oxfam Great Britain and is national country office for Oxfam International. Oxfam's program in Zambia builds on past learning and focuses on the following areas: improving the well-being of poor women and men, particularly those in rural areas; economic empowerment; access to essential services (education, health, and water); reducing the impact of disasters; promoting the rights of women.
Oxfam in Zambia works with partners in agriculture, holding government and the private sector accountable in the use of natural resources, women's rights and humanitarian help. Oxfam in Zambia is responsible for the implementation of the Sowing Diversity = Harvesting Security program in close collaboration with national organizations, particularly the Community Technology Development Trust (CTDT) and Zambia Alliance for Agroecology and Biodiversity (ZAAB).
